Save Everyone.name: Save Everyone
Save Everyone.description:
🆘 You want no one left behind: every civilian, every teammate, maybe even the villain.

💪 You know it is impossible, and you mean to try.
🧭 This motivation shapes the chances the story offers: rescues, triage and people who need you in time.
⚠️ Not every rescue succeeds, and saving one person can cost another.
Save Everyone.traitNarrativeEffects: The character measures success by who gets out alive. The narrator surfaces rescue opportunities: collapsed buildings, fires, floods, panicking crowds, bystanders hurt in villain attacks, Thirteen's rescue training at the USJ and rescue-focused agencies. It brings in rescue pros, paramedics, firefighters, victims and their families, and now and then a villain who might be worth saving. Pressures: triage, where saving one person costs another; the pull to break their own body for one more rescue; orders to pull back; and people they cannot reach in time. Not every rescue succeeds, and losses are never staged for shock: the character gets real chances and honest outcomes. The narrator never decides whom they try to save.
